ui-menus-controls.title: UI, menus and controls
ui-menus-controls.status: Read-only source review at 9f045ebca, report6566137785. Exact overlap with saves/world/art is counted on those pages once; multiplayer boundaries remain with #1609. Second review 6566596996 at 73741aa8 accounts for all 35 remaining declarations: U7 five proposed, U8/U9/U10 thirty kept; no overlap.
ui-menus-controls.keepSummary: input recovery, menu ownership, opening/travel handoff, retained diagnostics and valid creator/editor data
protections: Remapped keys, mouse and pad act once per press while Choose/Back retain recovery routes.
Only the top menu owns input; closing it cannot leave walking keys held or activate a hidden panel.
Travel and loading handoff preserve island, seed, settings and ownership.
Reports and replay diagnostics survive quotas and corrupt data without changing play.
Creator/editor controls produce valid data while historical comparison modes remain distinct.

groups.title: Preview and chart distribution thresholds
groups.reason: Bag previews compare total throws/hits across loops. ChartLayout samples three archipelagos and pins median/max bearing drift, radius growth and quadrant shares. Split those outcome thresholds while retaining bag reach, chart containment and patch exclusion.
groups.question: Split these three tests so sampled throw/hit and chart-distribution targets run as nonblocking reports? Yes keeps reach, containment, patch separation and repeatable preview behavior blocking.
examples: throws at its bag's rate: the Bumbag most, the Purse least
gives out at its bag's reach, landing letters on the creatures in reach: the far one only for the Purse
packs the islands over the whole disc: home in the middle, each near its bearing, later phases further out, each in its own patch
exampleLabels: Bag preview loops rank total letter counts.
Each bag preview must land a sampled hit.
Generated charts meet drift and quadrant-share targets.

groups.title: Controls, pause and menu recovery
groups.reason: Tests inject events/hosts and check input ownership, exception recovery, remaps and exactly-once actions. freezeStack replay equality is integrity despite advancing a game. Settings’ fixed recovery inputs are deliberate; controller tests do not measure GPU performance.
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
examples: cannot clear the last Choose or Back input on either device, but can remove surplus inputs
pause owns keys and pads, and held keyboard input cannot leak across a frame-free pause/resume
preserves native button and slider defaults inside pause, Settings and the potion lab
exampleLabels: Choose and Back retain a working recovery input.
Keys released in an overlay do not keep her walking.

groups.title: Opening, travel, progression and links
groups.reason: Known inputs drive fallback, saved tuning, temporary finds and loading completeness. Map/campaign cases compare retained identity rather than bot success. Existing W1/W6 cases are excluded from duplicate membership here. House reviewer verified three whatsNew tests: lazy/retry networking, safe bounded paths/data and batched ordered changelog transport.
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
examples: one going wrong loads its link as before

exampleLabels: A failed in-place journey can use its fallback link.

groups.title: Diagnostics, encoded data and queue bounds
groups.reason: Synthetic rows, fake timers and worker traces exercise bounded allocation, retained report text and transparent instrumentation. Long arrays and paused loops are integrity pressure, not gameplay outcome targets. S6 already contains recorded-game/comment replay and is not double-counted.
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
examples: rejects corrupt envelopes and expansion bombs before allocating frame arrays
keeps payload identity and original promises/results/errors when tracing is off
bounds durable debug growth across a long pause and reload while preserving warnings and errors
exampleLabels: Malformed or oversized diagnostic data is rejected.
Tracing preserves worker messages and results.

groups.title: Production-sized replay pressure fixture cost
groups.reason: Preserve legacy report text through duplicated replay pressure, reload and both exports. Coordinator report 6566569947 measured 24.7 s on a normal shard and a 30 s timeout on unrelated multiplayer head d7ce9a6e. This is fixture cost, not evidence against the safety assertion. Yes means use a smaller blocking integrity fixture and move only production-sized pressure to a nonblocking report; no means retain the current fixture. No implementation before Ed rules.
groups.question: Keep the report-integrity checks with a smaller blocking fixture and move production-sized pressure to a nonblocking report?
examples: preserves legacy report text through production-sized duplicated replay pressure, reload and both exports

groups.reason: Report sampled maximum angle changes, midpoint distance, smoothness multiplier and two-second travel magnitudes. Keep authored tables/poses, intro termination, no overshoot, capped look-ahead and settled tracking. coastCamera:38 and rules:788 require NEW direct finite/continuity and input-to-movement/camera-coupling coverage in the later implementation; they do not already contain separable integrity assertions. Report 6566596996 records each assertion disposition.

groups.title: Paused picture, clock and quality-controller policy
groups.reason: Keep no paused redraw, each changed title redraw once, paused clock and MAX_STEP clamp. Quality modes, nonfinite/skipped sample handling, pending loads, hysteresis and exponential retry are supplied-input policy contracts, not measured throughput outcomes.

groups.reason: Keep current morning order, bed gating, real kit/bag prerequisites and settled-win map/bed guidance. Waking is fixture preparation. rulings: Relaxed sea chart: the old comparison placed each island on its phase ring; Ed12Oct in island.md says ‘the rings can be very relaxed, a pleasing layout is much more important’ and ‘the phase rings should hardly show’. chartLayout:42 checks ringAt for the comparison tool’s before panel, not the live chart. Keep it; U1 targets the separate live-layout statistics.

Fixed interval replacement: DESIGN records old party.interval ‘5 minutes then1’ and 9Oct ‘Pure constant speed’. tuningPreset:15 copies a historical preset and explicitly notes the runtime no longer reads its interval. Its copy/unknown-preset/untouched-camera assertions protect compatibility, not retired wave pacing.

Opening replacement: the sea chart came first20Oct; Ed23Oct says ‘the first screen should be the witch waking up in her bedroom on the home island instead of the map’. Opening tests now check bedroom defaults plus documented opening=old/tool/resume exceptions. The old-decks comparison is expressly retained in house.md. End-card tests assert their26Oct removal.

Familiars: creator.test.ts:48 supplies old familiar data and asserts removal under Ed8Oct ‘Remove familiars’. It is migration protection. Controls tests assert the29Oct swap back, L2 dodge and correct d-pad zoom; no removed face-button layout was found required.

Nine beetle/shape-control cases are counted under art once, not UI twice. Report/replay cases already in S6 and identity/link cases already in W1/W6 remain there. U6’s36 owner-boundary tests are listing-only for1609.

Coordinator timing proposal 6566569947 refines U4: the report-integrity assertion remains blocking; only fixture scale and production-sized pressure reporting are proposed to change. Alternatives recorded by the coordinator include a looser per-test timeout.

Second review 6566596996: Ed 6 October gradual coast transition still applies, but sampled comfort is distinct from direct correctness. Bedroom-first opening retains generic seated intro camera math. 28 October pin behavior supersedes the stale hidden-at-target header; current assertions already match it. No obsolete whole behavior test found.
